[NO-SOURCE] Characterisations of the Nuer polity ('ordered anarchy', an 'acephalous kinship state', the leopard-skin chief as a sacred person without political authority) and of eastward expansion at Dinka expense were cited to Evans-Pritchard (1940) and are withdrawn pending a readable page-level source. Gleichen's 1905 compendium places Nuer on the Sobat and Baro from about 32° 33' to about 34° 10' E, and on the Zeraf island and right bank of the Zeraf to about opposite Shambe (GLEICHEN1905_V1 pp.132, 142). GHA VII says the Nuer by the Sobat and White Nile resisted the Condominium from Dengkur and Diu (d. 1906/1907) to the 'widespread Nuer revolt of 1927' (GHA VII ch.4, p.81).

Key events
  • Self-name Nath; c.200,000 people in the 1930s [NO-SOURCE]
  • Swamps and savannah on both sides of the Nile south of the Sobat/Bahr al-Ghazal junction and along both tributaries
  • Seasonal movement between villages and dry-season cattle camps

Culture

[NO-SOURCE] Statements on cattle-centred social life, ox-names, genealogies likened to 'an inventory of a kraal', and the adoption of captured Dinka boys were cited to Evans-Pritchard's 1930s ethnography and are withdrawn pending a readable page-level source.

Economy

Gleichen's 1905 compendium found the Nuer of the Sobat and Baro had 'little or no grain, living chiefly on fish', but 'numerous flocks of goats and sheep in the vicinity of Nasser Post, and also some magnificent herds of cattle at Ajungmir' (GLEICHEN1905_V1 p.134). Outsider, 1904–05 trade-report view. [NO-SOURCE] The 1930s characterisation (pre-eminently pastoral; more millet and maize than supposed; horticulture as toil forced by poverty of stock) was cited to Evans-Pritchard and is withdrawn.

«تدور معظم أنشطتهم الاجتماعية حول الماشية». وكثيراً ما يُنادى الرجال بأسماء ثيرانهم، وتتخذ النساء أسماء من الثيران والأبقار، و«قد تبدو سلسلة نسب النويري كأنها جرد لحظيرة». وكان الصبية الدينكا الأسرى يُتبنَّون عادة في سلالات آسريهم ويُعَدّون أبناء. إثنوغرافيا الثلاثينيات.
